+package gramaire.cli
+
+import gramaire.IR
+
+// `gramaire lint --target <name> <file>`: a preflight compat gate answering "will this grammar
+// survive export to this backend, and if not, what specifically breaks?" Deliberately reuses the
+// already-built IR (the same `Main.parseWithDocs` + `IR.buildIRP` pipeline `runEmit`/`runCheck`
+// already run) rather than re-parsing or re-deriving a parallel compatibility model — each check
+// below is a pure, located `Vector[String]` finding list against a resolved backend name, the
+// exact shape `GramaireCheck.GateResult` already uses for `check`'s own structure/drift gates.
+//
+// A first version, not an exhaustive compatibility auditor: three checks, each verified empirically
+// against the current backends rather than assumed from the notation's own docs.
+object GramaireLint:
+
+  // ANTLR4 has no precedence-declaration syntax at all — confirmed empirically:
+  // `BackendAntlr.scala` never reads `ir.grammar.precedence` anywhere, unlike `BackendBison.scala`,
+  // which DOES consume it to reconstruct `%left`/`%right`/`%nonassoc` (ADR D37/D38). A grammar with
+  // a non-empty `## Precedence` block silently loses every declared level on `--target antlr`
+  // export; Bison has no such gap.
+  def precedenceLoss(ir: IR, backendName: String): Vector[String] =
+    if backendName == "antlr" && ir.grammar.precedence.nonEmpty then
+      val levels = ir.grammar.precedence.sortBy(_.level).map(p => s"${p.assoc}@${p.level}")
+      Vector(
+        s"## Precedence declares ${ir.grammar.precedence.length} level(s) " +
+          s"(${levels.mkString(", ")}); ANTLR4 has no precedence-declaration syntax, so every " +
+          "level is silently dropped on export (Bison's `%left`/`%right`/`%nonassoc` has no such gap)"
+      )
+    else Vector.empty
+
+  // Confirmed empirically: NEITHER `BackendAntlr.scala` nor `BackendBison.scala` (nor any other
+  // first-party textual backend) reads `IRRule.delegate` at all — each backend's rule-rendering
+  // (`altText`) only ever looks at `r.rhs`, so a `-> name`/`-> name(args)` alternative (ADR D48)
+  // renders as a bare, actionless alt with no comment or reference to the delegate left behind; the
+  // delegate silently vanishes, not just its resolution. `ir` is the one exception — it serializes
+  // the whole IR (delegate included) as JSON, so nothing is lost exporting there.
+  def delegateLoss(ir: IR, backendName: String): Vector[String] =
+    if backendName == "ir" then Vector.empty
+    else
+      val ntNameById = ir.grammar.nonterminals.map(n => n.id -> n.name).toMap
+      ir.grammar.rules.collect {
+        case r if r.delegate.isDefined =>
+          val d = r.delegate.get
+          val rule = ntNameById.getOrElse(r.lhs, s"nt${r.lhs}")
+          val argsText = if d.args.isEmpty then "" else s"(${d.args.mkString(", ")})"
+          s"rule `$rule` delegates its action to `-> ${d.name}$argsText`; the '$backendName' " +
+            "backend never renders a rule's delegate at all, so the reference vanishes on " +
+            "export, not even as a comment"
+      }
+
+  // Confirmed empirically (same grep as `delegateLoss`): `IR.externals` (ADR D49's `## Externals`
+  // embedded fenced implementations) is referenced by no first-party textual backend either — an
+  // author who embedded a delegate's real `-> name` implementation directly in the `.gram.md` gets
+  // it silently dropped too, on top of the reference itself (`delegateLoss`). Scoped the same way:
+  // `ir` carries it through as JSON, so it alone is exempt.
+  def externalsLoss(ir: IR, backendName: String): Vector[String] =
+    if backendName == "ir" || ir.externals.isEmpty then Vector.empty
+    else
+      ir.externals.map { ext =>
+        val langs = ext.impl.keys.toVector.sorted.mkString(", ")
+        s"## Externals embeds a `$langs` implementation for `${ext.name}`; the '$backendName' " +
+          "backend carries none of it into the export — the embedded code vanishes along with " +
+          "the delegate reference that names it"
+      }
+
+  /** All of `lint`'s checks against `ir` for the named target backend, one `GateResult` per check —
+    * mirrors `GramaireCheck.checkStructure`/`checkDrift`'s pass-is-empty convention exactly, so
+    * `runLint` can present them the same way `runCheck` presents its own gates.
+    */
+  def gates(ir: IR, backendName: String): Vector[GramaireCheck.GateResult] =
+    Vector(
+      GramaireCheck.GateResult("precedence", precedenceLoss(ir, backendName)),
+      GramaireCheck.GateResult("delegate", delegateLoss(ir, backendName)),
+      GramaireCheck.GateResult("externals", externalsLoss(ir, backendName))
+    )

+  /** Options for `lint`: the single positional grammar file and the required `--target` backend
+    * name — deliberately its own small type (not a reuse of `EmitOpts`) since `lint` has neither
+    * `--out` nor `--strategy`, and its backend flag is named `--target` (the backend it's asking

+    * with).

+  final case class LintOpts(file: Option[String], target: Option[String])
+
+  private val defaultLint: LintOpts = LintOpts(None, None)
+
+  /** Parse `lint`'s arguments: the single positional grammar file and `--target <name>` — same
+    * recursive-descent shape as `parseEmit`/`parseExplain`.
+    */
+  def parseLint(args: Vector[String]): Either[String, LintOpts] =
+    def go(opts: LintOpts, rest: Vector[String]): Either[String, LintOpts] =
+      rest.headOption match
+        case None => Right(opts)
+        case Some(a) =>
+          val tail = rest.tail
+          a match
+            case "--target" => value("--target", tail)((v, r) => go(opts.copy(target = Some(v)), r))
+            case _ if a.startsWith("--") => Left(s"unknown option: $a")
+            case _ =>

+                case Some(_) => Left(s"unexpected extra argument: $a")
+                case None    => go(opts.copy(file = Some(a)), tail)

+        k: (String, Vector[String]) => Either[String, LintOpts]
+    ): Either[String, LintOpts] =
+      rest.headOption match
+        case Some(v) => k(v, rest.tail)
+        case None    => Left(s"$name requires a value")
+    go(defaultLint, args)
+

+  // `runEmit`'s own parse-then-build-IR pipeline (`parseWithDocs` + `IR.buildIRP`, so `## Externals`

+  // pathway, then runs `GramaireLint.gates` against the resolved backend and presents them exactly
+  // the way `runCheck` presents its own structure/drift gates. Exit code mirrors `check`'s
+  // convention: non-zero if any gate reports a finding, so it's scriptable as a CI preflight.
+  private def runLint(args: Vector[String]): Unit =
+    parseLint(args) match
+      case Left(e) => die(s"lint: $e")
+      case Right(opts) =>
+        (opts.file, opts.target) match
+          case (None, _) => die("lint: no grammar file given")

+          case (Some(file), Some(target)) =>

+                            val spans = Lr.spanIndexOf(md)

+                              s"lint: $file has unresolved LR(1) conflicts:\n\n" +
+                                renderDiags(
+                                  Diagnostics.conflictDiagnostics(g, spans, conflicts),
+                                  file,
+                                  md
+                                )
+                            )
+                          case Right(ir) =>
+                            val gates = GramaireLint.gates(ir, target)
+                            val base = Path.of(file).getFileName
+                            println(s"gramaire lint --target $target $base\n")
+                            var findingCount = 0
+                            for gt <- gates do
+                              if gt.failures.isEmpty then println(s"  PASS  ${gt.name}")
+                              else
+                                findingCount += gt.failures.length
+                                println(s"  FAIL  ${gt.name}")
+                                gt.failures.foreach(f => println(s"        - $f"))
+                            println("")
+                            println(
+                              if findingCount == 0 then s"lint clean: $target survives export."
+                              else s"lint found $findingCount issue(s) exporting to $target."
+                            )
+                            if findingCount > 0 then sys.exit(1)
+

+package gramaire.cli
+
+import gramaire.*
+import gramaire.Sym.*
+
+// Covers `GramaireLint`'s pure compat checks — the same hand-built-`Grammar`-plus-`IR.buildIR(P)`
+// shape `BackendAntlrSuite`/`BackendBisonSuite` already use for their own backend-emission
+// assertions, since `GramaireLint.gates` is itself just IR-in, findings-out. `Main.parseLint`'s
+// argument parsing is covered alongside `parseEmit`/`parseExplain` in `MainSuite`.
+class GramaireLintSuite extends munit.FunSuite:
+
+  private val precGrammar = Grammar(
+    Vector(
+      Rule(
+        "Expr",
+        Vector.empty,
+        Vector(
+          Alt(Vector(Ref("Expr"), Lit("+"), Ref("Expr")), None, None),
+          Alt(Vector(Ref("NUM")), None, None)
+        )
+      )
+    )
+  )
+
+  private val prec = Precedence(Map("+" -> Prec(0, Assoc.LeftA)))
+
+  private val delegateGrammar = Grammar(
+    Vector(
+      Rule(
+        "Expr",
+        Vector.empty,
+        Vector(
+          Alt(
+            Vector(Ref("NUM"), Lit("+"), Ref("NUM")),
+            None,
+            None,
+            Some(DelegateSpec("Add", Vector.empty))
+          ),
+          Alt(Vector(Ref("NUM")), None, None)
+        )
+      )
+    )
+  )
+
+  private val cleanGrammar = Grammar(
+    Vector(Rule("Expr", Vector.empty, Vector(Alt(Vector(Ref("NUM")), None, None))))
+  )
+
+  test("precedenceLoss: a non-empty ## Precedence is reported lost against --target antlr") {
+    IR.buildIRP(prec, Method.Canonical, "P", precGrammar) match
+      case Left(e) => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) =>
+        val findings = GramaireLint.precedenceLoss(ir, "antlr")
+        assert(findings.nonEmpty, "expected a precedence-loss finding")
+        assert(findings.head.contains("Precedence"))
+  }
+
+  test("precedenceLoss: the same grammar reports clean against --target bison") {
+    IR.buildIRP(prec, Method.Canonical, "P", precGrammar) match
+      case Left(e)   => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) => assertEquals(GramaireLint.precedenceLoss(ir, "bison"), Vector.empty)
+  }
+
+  test("precedenceLoss: a grammar with no precedence reports clean against antlr") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", cleanGrammar) match
+      case Left(e)   => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) => assertEquals(GramaireLint.precedenceLoss(ir, "antlr"), Vector.empty)
+  }
+
+  test("delegateLoss: a rule with a `-> name` delegate is reported lost against antlr") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", delegateGrammar) match
+      case Left(e) => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) =>
+        val findings = GramaireLint.delegateLoss(ir, "antlr")
+        assert(findings.nonEmpty, "expected a delegate-loss finding")
+        assert(findings.head.contains("Add"), findings.head)
+        assert(findings.head.contains("Expr"), findings.head)
+  }
+
+  test("delegateLoss: the same grammar is also reported lost against bison") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", delegateGrammar) match
+      case Left(e)   => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) => assert(GramaireLint.delegateLoss(ir, "bison").nonEmpty)
+  }
+
+  test("delegateLoss: the `ir` backend is exempt (it serializes the delegate as JSON)") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", delegateGrammar) match
+      case Left(e)   => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) => assertEquals(GramaireLint.delegateLoss(ir, "ir"), Vector.empty)
+  }
+
+  test("delegateLoss: a grammar with no delegate reports clean") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", cleanGrammar) match
+      case Left(e)   => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) => assertEquals(GramaireLint.delegateLoss(ir, "antlr"), Vector.empty)
+  }
+
+  test("externalsLoss: an embedded implementation is reported lost against a textual backend") {
+    val g = delegateGrammar.copy(externals =
+      Vector(GrammarExternal("Add", Map("javascript" -> "(c) => c[0] + c[2]")))
+    )
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", g) match
+      case Left(e) => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) =>
+        val findings = GramaireLint.externalsLoss(ir, "bison")
+        assert(findings.nonEmpty, "expected an externals-loss finding")
+        assert(findings.head.contains("Add"), findings.head)
+  }
+
+  test("externalsLoss: no `## Externals` section reports clean") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", delegateGrammar) match
+      case Left(e)   => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) => assertEquals(GramaireLint.externalsLoss(ir, "bison"), Vector.empty)
+  }
+
+  test("gates: a grammar with neither issue reports every gate clean (would exit 0)") {
+    IR.buildIR(Method.Canonical, "P", cleanGrammar) match
+      case Left(e) => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) =>
+        val gates = GramaireLint.gates(ir, "antlr")
+        assert(gates.forall(_.failures.isEmpty), gates.toString)
+  }
+
+  test("gates: a precedence-losing grammar fails exactly the precedence gate against antlr") {
+    IR.buildIRP(prec, Method.Canonical, "P", precGrammar) match
+      case Left(e) => fail(s"should build: $e")
+      case Right(ir) =>
+        val gates = GramaireLint.gates(ir, "antlr")
+        val byName = gates.map(g => g.name -> g.failures.nonEmpty).toMap
+        assertEquals(byName, Map("precedence" -> true, "delegate" -> false, "externals" -> false))
+  }

@@ -746,6 +746,7 @@ everything target-specific is independent.
 | D47 | Sigil de-Yacc-ification: `%` → `name:`/`lang:`/`->`/`@` | **Settings-fence directives become YAML-style `key: value`: `%name X` → `name: X`, `%lang X` → `lang: X`. Token-line modifiers split by provenance: `%skip` → `-> skip` (ANTLR4's own `-> command` lexer-command syntax, borrowed verbatim — a bare `skip` names the one builtin command); `%external(pass)` → `-> <name>` (folds into the SAME arrow family: `->` followed by any identifier other than the literal word `skip` names a host post-lex pass, bare identifier, no parens); `%caseless` → `@caseless`; `%prec N` → `@prec(N)` (parens now, unlike the old two-word form). `%left`/`%right`/`%nonassoc` in `## Precedence` fences are explicitly UNCHANGED — real Bison syntax, out of scope.** | `%` is specifically a Yacc/Bison-ism that ANTLR4 doesn't share at all — ANTLR4 uses bare keyword blocks, `@`-action-blocks, `$`-references, and its own `-> command` lexer-command syntax — so keeping `%` project-wide bought no real ANTLR4 familiarity, only accidental Bison lineage. The redesign splits directives into "genuinely borrowed, matching real target syntax 1:1" (`-> skip` from ANTLR4; `%left`/`%right`/`%nonassoc` staying as real Bison syntax) versus "Gramaire's own invention, honestly marked as such" (`@caseless`, `@prec(N)`, `-> <name>` for external passes — this last one reuses the arrow container for a non-ANTLR4 concept, but was judged acceptable since Gramaire's own `.gram.md` files are never fed directly to real antlr4/bison anyway; full interop always goes through the IR/converters per D43's positioning). This avoids the "fake compatibility" trap of a sigil implying a semantic match that isn't real. |
 | D48 | Alternative delegate slot: `-> IDENT` / `-> IDENT(args...)` | **A rule alternative's trailing slot grows a sixth shape: `-> IDENT` delegates that alternative's action to a named implementation, instead of an inline `{% %}`/`{%? %}` action. `Alt` (Core AST) becomes a flat, epsilon-free six-alternative cross-product — `SymList Label Action \| SymList Label Delegate \| SymList Label \| SymList Action \| SymList Delegate \| SymList` — never a wrapper nonterminal with an empty alternative (same epsilon-free discipline as D27). A new reserved `ARROW` token (`"->"`) joins the Core's own lexis at the same level as `PLUS`/`STAR`/`LANGLE`/`RANGLE`/`COMMA`; confirmed zero collision risk empirically, since a bare `-`/`->` had no prior meaning anywhere in the notation's own vocabulary (an unquoted `-` was an "unexpected character" lex error before this). Extended in the same phase's direct follow-up with a parenthesized, comma-separated argument list — `Delegate : ARROW IDENT \| ARROW IDENT '(' ArgList ')'`, `ArgList : Arg \| ArgList ',' Arg` (left-recursive, matching the notation's own house style for comma lists, reusing the `COMMA` token already declared for macro-call `Args`), `Arg : IDENT \| TERM_LIT \| NUMBER` — enabling host commands like `-> channel(HIDDEN)`, `-> type(TOKEN_TYPE)`, or arbitrary custom ones like `-> my_custom(arg1, arg2, 42)`. A new reserved `NUMBER` token (`/[0-9]+/`) joins the lexis for the bare-number argument shape; the core `lr`-notation lexer had no numeric token class before this (not to be confused with `Tokens.scala`'s separate bespoke token-LINE parser, a different lexer). `Alt.delegate` changed from `Option[String]` to `Option[DelegateSpec]` (`case class DelegateSpec(name: String, args: Vector[String])`, `args` empty for the bare form) and `IRRule.delegate` from `Option[String]` to `Option[IRDelegate]` (mirroring exactly) — a breaking shape change to a field that had not shipped to any real-world consumer yet, so modifying rather than versioning it was judged acceptable. Each argument is carried through as its own literal source text (an identifier's name, a literal's unescaped content, or a number's digit string) — the IR never interprets it further. Mutually exclusive with an action by construction, not a runtime check (the grammar has no production combining both, so writing both is a parse error). Verified conflict-free under Canonical/LALR/IELR, including in `Gramaire.gram.md` (the full-notation meta-grammar), which already had its own `ARROW` token for `-> skip`/`-> pass` lexer-command modifiers and safely reuses it here since the two occur in disjoint rule contexts.** | Delegating an alternative's action to something named rather than inlined is the natural next step once actions exist as a slot at all (D3/D25) — a consumer application (or, in a later phase, a fenced implementation elsewhere in the same file) can supply the real implementation, without forcing every action into `{% %}` source text. Parameterization followed immediately once the bare form landed, since a real delegate target (a lexer channel, a token-type override, a custom host command) almost always needs at least one argument to be useful — deferring it would have meant re-deriving the same `Alt`/`IRRule` field-shape change a second time. Scoped narrowly this phase: only the syntax + IR field land; resolving the name (consumer-supplied lookup now, fenced-implementation lookup later) is explicitly deferred to the `## Externals` phase, which is a separate, later piece of work. Mirrors D42's predicate field precedent exactly for the IR-additive-field mechanics (encode/decode/validate/schema, goldens byte-unchanged when absent). |
 | D49 | `## Externals`: embedded fenced implementations for a `-> name` delegate | **A new OPTIONAL reserved H2, `## Externals` (ADR D29's "a nonterminal, or a reserved section" list gains a fifth member), holding one `### <name>` H3 subsection per delegate name, each with one or more real-language-tagged fences (` ```javascript `, ` ```rust `, …  — genuine host code, never a bare ` ```gramaire ` content-shape fence) providing that name's implementation body; one fence per target profile when an author embeds more than one. Canonical position: after the rule sections and the optional `## Precedence`, before the optional `## Error messages` and the always-present `## Generated tables` (`GramaireCheck.scala`'s `alwaysTail`/canonical-order check). A `-> name`/`-> name(args)` delegate (D48/D48-args) is now resolved, in order, by an embedded `### name` implementation here if present, else a consumer-supplied one at runtime (unchanged default). Purely additive: a grammar with zero `->` delegates needs no `## Externals` section, and a grammar with delegates doesn't have to define any of them here either. A `### name` with no fenced implementation inside it is a hard, located parse error (`Lr.parseWith`/`parse` themselves, not just an opt-in extractor); a `### name` defined but never referenced by any `-> name` is a warning, not an error (mirrors `unusedTokenWarnings`'s "warn on likely-unused, never hard-fail on merely unused" house style); the opposite shape — a `-> name` with no matching `### name` — is unchanged, unwarned, default behavior. `Grammar` gains `externals: Vector[GrammarExternal]` (`GrammarExternal(name, impl: Map[lang, code])`), populated the same way `Rule.doc` is (ADR D39): never by `Lr.parseWith`/`parse` themselves (so a self-hosted parse stays exactly equal to `Bootstrap.bootstrapGrammar`), only by the explicit `Lr.withExternals`/`parseWithDocs` opt-in. The IR gains a matching top-level, additive-when-non-empty `externals: Vector[IRExternal]` (`irVersion` stays 0) alongside `grammar`/`tables`/`conflicts` — document-level, not per-rule (unlike `delegate`, which lives on `IRRule`).** | The natural next step once D48/D48-args shipped the delegate *name* but deferred resolving it: an author who wants a grammar to be genuinely self-contained (no external wiring step) can now embed the implementation directly, while a consumer who'd rather supply it at runtime (a shared library of named handlers across many grammars, say) still can — the two resolution paths compose, they don't compete. Reusing `Rule.doc`'s exact opt-in-attachment shape (rather than baking `externals` into the self-hosted `lr` grammar itself) keeps this a bespoke document-structure/parsing concern layered on top of the notation, not a new core-grammar production — `Bootstrap.scala`'s actual productions, the self-host oracle, and the `Lr`-self-hosting goldens are all untouched, matching D29's "###+ is free presentational grouping" scoping (the `### name` subsections are validated by `Lr.parseWith` directly, not by the `##`-only structure gate). Mirrors D42/D48's additive-IR-field mechanics exactly (encode/decode/validate/schema, goldens byte-unchanged when absent). |
+| D50 | `gramaire lint --target <name>`: export-compat preflight | **A new CLI command, `gramaire lint --target <backend> <file>`, answering "will this grammar survive export to this backend, and if not, what specifically breaks?" — deliberately reusing the existing parse/IR-build/diagnostics pipeline (`Main.parseWithDocs` + `IR.buildIRP`, the same one `emit`/`check` already run) rather than a third, parallel compatibility model. `GramaireLint.gates(ir, backendName)` runs a small, first-version check set as `GramaireCheck.GateResult`s (mirroring `check`'s own structure/drift gate presentation, PASS/FAIL per gate with located `-` detail lines, non-zero exit on any finding — the same CI-scriptable convention `check` already uses): (1) **precedence loss** — confirmed empirically that `BackendAntlr.scala` never reads `ir.grammar.precedence` at all (ANTLR4 has no precedence-declaration syntax), while `BackendBison.scala` DOES consume it (D37/D38) — a non-empty `## Precedence` silently vanishes only on `--target antlr`; (2) **delegate loss** — confirmed empirically that NEITHER `BackendAntlr` nor `BackendBison` (nor any other first-party textual backend) reads `IRRule.delegate` (D48) at all: a `-> name` alternative renders as a bare actionless alt, the reference gone without even a comment; (3) **externals loss** — confirmed empirically that `IR.externals` (D49's embedded fenced implementations) is likewise read by no textual backend, so an author's embedded real-language code vanishes right along with the reference that names it. All three checks exempt the `ir` backend, which serializes the whole IR (delegate/externals included) as JSON and so loses nothing. Scoped deliberately narrow for a first version — three real, empirically-verified checks, not a speculative exhaustive compatibility auditor.** | The natural next step once export-lossy gaps existed silently (D38's "predicates/actions dropped on Bison import" and this phase's own delegate/externals findings) without any preflight surface to ask about them before running `emit` and discovering the loss after the fact. Reusing `runCheck`'s presentation shape (not `runEmit`'s "write files" shape, and explicitly NOT `runImport`'s bare-string-to-stderr anti-pattern — no location, no structure) keeps the CLI's diagnostic surface consistent rather than growing a fourth ad hoc reporting style.
